newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Maag plans more sales of units in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Maag plans more sales of units in 1997.

text.p: Maag Holding AG said it planned to sell its Schmid Gruppe and Maag France divisions this year as it continues its strategy of withdrawing from industrial activity and focusing on industrial and real estate holdings.
Chairman and chief executive Samuel Gartmann also told a news conference the company expected to post a group profit of 14 million Swiss francs on turnover of 14 million as well.
Maag earned 28 million in 1996 on net sales of 91 million after losing 50 million in 1995 on sales of 379 million.
Maag has built 55 million in reserves to cover the sale of Schmid, Maag France and other units already sold.
Finance director Peter Wuersch said it would be wrong to hope these reserves would not be used.

Company officials said asset sales would be completed around mid-year but gave no other details. Proceeds will be used to reduce debt, which dropped to 76 million last year from 299 million in 1995. Debt should be eliminated by the end of 1997.
